learning_objectives.objective: Understand the anatomy of the upper and lower airways.
Identify key anatomical landmarks relevant for airway procedures.
Recognize common anatomical variants and their implications.

key_points.point: The larynx is crucial for phonation, respiration, and aspiration prevention.
Knowledge of airway anatomy is essential for interventional pulmonology.
The Mallampati classification helps assess airway access difficulty.

steps.description: Position the patient appropriately, usually in the sniffing position.
critical_points: Ensure the head is extended and neck flexed.
Use a bag-mask ventilation if necessary.

steps.description: Insert the laryngoscope blade into the mouth and sweep the tongue to the left.
Insert the endotracheal tube through the vocal cords.
critical_points: Confirm placement by auscultation and capnography.

tables.clinical_relevance: Essential for understanding bronchial anatomy during procedures.

boxes.title: Clinical Pearl
boxes.content: The cricoid cartilage is a critical landmark for emergency airway access.

definitions.definition: A system used to predict the difficulty of intubation based on the visibility of oropharyngeal structures.

summary.chapter_summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of airway anatomy, emphasizing its importance in clinical practice, particularly in interventional pulmonology.
clinical_pearls: Understanding airway anatomy is crucial for successful intubation and bronchoscopy.
The cricoid cartilage serves as a landmark for emergency procedures.
practice_recommendations: Regularly review airway anatomy to enhance procedural skills.
Utilize classification systems like Mallampati to assess airway difficulty.
summary.future_directions: Further research into anatomical variations and their clinical implications is needed.
